name: Pale periwinkle
lede: Pale periwinkle is a soft lavender-blue, the pale tone Robert Ridgway charted beside the parent color Periwinkle in his 1912 color atlas, decades before the plain name Periwinkle itself was recorded.

sections.title: A pale tone of Periwinkle
sections.body:
Pale periwinkle puts Ridgway's tone word Pale in front of [[periwinkle]], the paired-tone method his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* used across the atlas [1]. The plain name Periwinkle only entered Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* in 1922, a decade later, and was later filed by the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 in block 203 [1]. Some library sources also use Pale periwinkle as an alternate label for [[pale-periwinkle]] and [[pallid-blue-violet]], names this close in color often double up in the record [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[pallid-blue-violet]], 3.6 units off and bluer than this swatch [1]; [[pale-wistaria-blue]] sits the same distance away, almost the same color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, 0.01 percent, as photographed, rarer than 79 percent of the named colors in our library [2]. In all three it plays a mid-value color by lightness rank [2]. The earliest match dates to 1516, in a work by Sebastiano del Piombo, a floor and not a first since the archive's early centuries are thin; that is 396 years before the name's 1912 record, so the match marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment [2].

In printed English the general word periwinkle (covering the plant and the sea snail along with any color sense) peaked in the 1870s, well before Ridgway's 1912 atlas, a reminder that an early Ngram count is catching the word, not this specific swatch [2].
